knowledge_gaps: The sampler is underspecified: title tokenization, similarity measure and band, pool size, missing-title fallback, negative count, recency distribution, and short-history handling need explicit definitions.

Terminal batches change both target selection and loss. Without a terminal-mask baseline retaining the original loss, improvements cannot be attributed to recency or confusable negatives. The 25% mined-negative loss cap also needs a precise weighting formula.

Title similarity does not establish model difficulty or incompatibility. Mining may penalize substitutes or reinforce lexical shortcuts; excluding observed training positives cannot eliminate false negatives.
Diagnostic comparisons require fixed masked examples and a fixed negative distribution across experiments. Otherwise, changing the sampler changes the measured margins independently of model quality.

The report lacks baseline validation HR@10, a budgeted ablation and checkpoint-selection schedule, and uncertainty estimates. Originality 4/10 is plausible, but potential 8/10 and difficulty 5/10 remain subjective without measured gains or implementation costs.

follow_up_queries.reason: Clarify whether title-based confusability is useful negative supervision and identify reproducible safeguards against false negatives and lexical shortcuts.
follow_up_queries.query: In BERT4Rec or masked sequential recommendation, what evidence supports lexical title-similarity negative sampling without pretrained embeddings? Look for reproducible similarity bands, random/hard mixture weighting, missing-text fallbacks, and false-negative controls, distinguishing lexical similarity from model-score hardness.

follow_up_queries.reason: Separate training alignment from loss changes and specify the proposed objective well enough to reproduce.
follow_up_queries.query: For BERT4Rec with random Cloze training and appended-mask next-item inference, how should terminal-prefix sampling and recency-biased endpoint selection be implemented and ablated? Compare retaining masked-item cross-entropy with pairwise softplus loss, including negative-count normalization and explicit hard-negative loss weights.

follow_up_queries.reason: Assess validation reliability and prevent sampler-dependent diagnostics or repeated configuration selection from producing misleading conclusions.
follow_up_queries.query: For sequential recommendation evaluated on 200 validation users per dataset with 99 fixed unique negatives and macro-average HR@10 across four datasets, what methods quantify paired improvement and validation-selection uncertainty? Include fixed-negative diagnostic comparisons, sampled-versus-full-catalog ranking limitations, and budget-limited checkpoint selection.
